# Simple plots

::: {.callout-note}
## Video
Coming soon.
:::

**In this chapter:** a histogram, a box plot and a scatter plot, with proper axis labels.

```{r}
morph <- read.csv("data/morphometry.csv")
morph$Height <- morph$Height / 10
morph$HandLength <- morph$HandLength / 10
```

Plot your data before you analyse it. Plots show patterns, and mistakes, that numbers hide.

## One variable: histogram

```{r}
hist(morph$Height, xlab = "Height (cm)", main = "")
```

Each bar shows how many people fall in a range of heights. Look at the shape: is it roughly symmetric, or are there two peaks?

`xlab` sets the axis label. `main = ""` removes the title, which a figure caption usually replaces.

## A number by group: box plot

```{r}
boxplot(Height ~ Sex, data = morph, ylab = "Height (cm)")
```

The `~` (tilde) means "explained by": height explained by sex. The thick line is the median, the box holds the middle half of the data.

## Two numbers: scatter plot

```{r}
plot(Height ~ HandLength, data = morph,
     xlab = "Hand length (cm)", ylab = "Height (cm)")
```

Each point is one person. Look at the direction and strength of the pattern, and for points far from the rest.

The same `y ~ x` formula appears again in the next two chapters. Learn it once and it carries through.

## Save a plot

In the Plots pane: Export > Save as Image.

## Functions in this chapter

- `hist()`: histogram of one number.
- `boxplot(y ~ group)`: a number by group.
- `plot(y ~ x)`: scatter plot of two numbers.
- `xlab`, `ylab`, `main`: axis labels and title.

## Your turn

Using `chirps.csv`, make a scatter plot of temperature against chirps per second, with clear axis labels and units. Which variable should go on the x-axis?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Model answer

```r
chirps <- read.csv("data/chirps.csv")
plot(temperature ~ chirps, data = chirps,
     xlab = "Chirps per second", ylab = "Temperature (°F)")
```

Chirps go on the x-axis because we use the chirp rate to predict the temperature. Warmer air goes with faster chirping.
:::
